questions.stemEn: A child has an accessory tragus. Which syndrome is known to be associated with this anomaly?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يربط accessory tragus بـoculoauriculovertebral syndrome (Goldenhar syndrome)، مع إمكانية ظهوره أيضًا في syndromes أخرى.
questions.reasoningEn: Accessory tragi are a recognized feature of oculoauriculovertebral/Goldenhar syndrome in the source.
questions.clinicalPearl: Accessory tragi may be isolated or syndromic; look for associated facial, ear and vertebral anomalies.

image.sourceRef: Accessory tragus image in Genetics Q26
image.captionEn: Original source image shows an accessory tragus.

tts.text: A child has an accessory tragus. Which syndrome is known to be associated with this anomaly? A. Goldenhar syndrome.

questions.stemEn: A child has broad thumbs and broad great toes in the provided picture. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationAr: Broad thumbs and great toes هي clue كلاسيكية في المصدر لـRubinstein-Taybi syndrome.
questions.reasoningEn: The diagnosis in the recalled source is based on the characteristic broad thumbs and great toes.
questions.clinicalPearl: Image morphology is central to this question; do not publish without the original/public-safe visual.

questions.stemEn: A child with hemihyperplasia is shown. Which test should be ordered frequently during follow-up?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار abdominal ultrasound بشكل متكرر لمراقبة Wilms tumor risk في isolated hemihyperplasia، ويذكر every 3 months through age 8 years في المرجع الذي استند إليه.
questions.reasoningEn: The source uses serial renal/abdominal ultrasonography for Wilms tumor surveillance in isolated hemihyperplasia.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Chest X-ray لا يراقب renal tumor، وCT المتكرر يعرّض الطفل للإشعاع ولا يُستخدم كscreening routine في المصدر.
questions.clinicalPearl: Tumor-surveillance intervals are guideline-sensitive and should be verified before publication.

tts.text: A child with hemihyperplasia is shown. Which test should be ordered frequently during follow-up? A. Chest X-ray. B. Abdominal CT. C. Abdominal ultrasound.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection 4th Ed 2026
sourceRefs.notes: Similar to PREP 2012 Q217; source gives renal ultrasound every 3 months through age 8, some through puberty.

questions.stemEn: A 14-year-old boy has unexplained intellectual disability, large ears and large testes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار Fragile X syndrome اعتمادًا على intellectual disability مع large ears وmacroorchidism.
questions.reasoningEn: Large ears and macroorchidism in an adolescent boy with intellectual disability are classic Fragile X clues in the source.
questions.clinicalPearl: Fragile X is associated with FMR1 CGG repeat expansion.

tts.text: A fourteen-year-old boy has unexplained intellectual disability, large ears and large testes. What is the most likely diagnosis? A. Fragile X syndrome.

questions.stemEn: A 14-year-old boy with unexplained intellectual disability has more than 200 CGG repeats in the FMR1 gene. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationAr: وجود >200 CGG repeats في FMR1 gene هو full mutation pattern الذي يطابق Fragile X syndrome في المصدر.
questions.reasoningEn: The source identifies an FMR1 CGG repeat expansion over 200 as Fragile X syndrome.
questions.clinicalPearl: Premutation and full-mutation ranges have different clinical and counseling implications.

tts.text: A fourteen-year-old boy with unexplained intellectual disability has more than two hundred CGG repeats in the FMR1 gene. What is the most likely diagnosis? A. Fragile X syndrome.

questions.stemEn: A child with Waardenburg syndrome is shown. Which finding is associated with this condition?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يربط Waardenburg syndrome بـsensorineural deafness، ولذلك الإجابة A.
questions.reasoningEn: Hearing loss is a recognized feature of Waardenburg syndrome in the source.
questions.clinicalPearl: Waardenburg combines pigmentary features with variable congenital sensorineural hearing loss.

questions.stemEn: A child with Waardenburg syndrome is shown. Which system should be examined?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار hearing assessment لأن congenital hearing loss من أهم associations في Waardenburg syndrome.
questions.reasoningEn: Hearing evaluation is prioritized because sensorineural hearing loss is a major Waardenburg feature.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Vision ليس الاختيار الذي يركز عليه المصدر في هذا السؤال.
questions.clinicalPearl: Early hearing assessment matters because intervention affects speech and language development.

questions.reasoningEn: Butterfly vertebrae are a classic skeletal association of Alagille syndrome in the source.
questions.clinicalPearl: Alagille syndrome can include cholestasis, characteristic facies, peripheral pulmonary stenosis and butterfly vertebrae.
